title: How to Perform a Data Readiness Review for Space ML
description: A practical method for deciding whether a dataset is adequate before developing or verifying an ML component for a space system — with a checklist and a satellite-telemetry example.
author: Embedded AI & ML Verification Engineer (portfolio author)
seoTitle: Data Readiness Review for Space ML — Engineering Note
seoDescription: How to decide if a dataset is ready for space-ML development: quality, representativeness, leakage and review.

content.text: An ML component for a space system inherits the weaknesses of its data. If the training and verification data do not represent the intended operating conditions, no amount of model tuning can repair the gap. A data readiness review is the gate that prevents modelling from starting on unsuitable data.

Define first what the ML will be used for, where it will run, and which failures matter. The intended use decides which data properties are critical: a false positive may be tolerable for a triage aid but unacceptable for an autonomous action.

items: Record dataset name, version and content hash (SHA-256).
Record origin, generator or acquisition campaign.
State clearly whether data are real, simulated, synthetic or augmented.

content.text: Freeze a data dictionary: column semantics, units of measurement, timestamp format, sampling frequency and allowed categorical values. Type mismatches are cheap to fix now and expensive after modelling.

Quantity missingness per column and per row. Decide an explicit policy: drop, impute, or model missingness as a feature. A column that is missing in 30% of training samples but 2% at inference behaves differently in operation.
Duplicate rows inflate apparent sample size and distort class priors. Detect exact and near-duplicate rows, and distinguish legitimate repeated samples from export artefacts.
An outlier is a possible statistical anomaly, not automatically an error. Engineering review decides whether an outlier is a sensor fault, a calibration flag, or a rare legitimate event.
If the dataset is for supervised ML, the target must be defined operationally: what exactly is an anomaly, who labelled it, and with which rules?
Measure the majority/minority ratio. A balanced dataset is not automatically representative: balancing changes priors and may hide the true operational distribution.

items: Check time span, cadence and gaps.
Correlate large gaps with acquisition events before imputing.

content.text: Map each Operational Design Domain condition to the dataset. Mark coverage as verified, partial or missing. If a condition cannot be represented, that is a finding, not an assumption.

Look for duplicated samples across splits, target-derived features, identifiers used as features, and preprocessing fitted on the test set. Leakage indicators are heuristics: they require engineering confirmation, and they can make metrics misleadingly optimistic.
Separate training, validation and test sets before any model work. On time series, random splits can leak the future into the past: prefer temporal or grouped splits when the signal is sequential.
Link dataset versions to requirements and later to model versions. An assurance record must be able to answer: which data produced which model, and which tests used which dataset.
A weighted score over quality categories is useful as a decision-support indicator. It is not a substitute for review: it does not know the mission.
A human reviewer issues the final decision: Ready, Conditionally Ready, or Not Ready, with explicit conditions when applicable.

items: Statistical quality is not operational fitness.
A score does not replace mission review.
Synthetic data must always be identified as such.
Schema, units and timestamp format frozen

content.text: In the Telemetry Anomaly Detector project, the review covered nominal, known-anomaly, unseen-anomaly, missing-channel, drift and noise subsets. The score reached 94 with full coverage, but the review decision remained Conditionally Ready: the unseen and drift subsets were under-represented, and a balanced-looking class distribution hid the real 2.5% anomaly prior.

A data readiness review turns 'we have data' into 'we have data that supports this ML component for this intended use'. The method is tool-agnostic and applies to any engineering workflow that treats ML as a verifiable component.

items: Guidance concepts inspired by ECSS-E-HB-40-02A (handbook; no certification implied).
